basis.governing_question: How can Grupo Vale integrate sales, purchasing and finance of its three acquired regional food distributors into its own, starting with the first company?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Assess how sales, purchasing and finance run at each acquired company and where they differ from Grupo Vale.

gate.label: Go/no-go on design
gate.decision: Go ahead with design on the agreed priority gaps in sales, purchasing and finance?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define how each acquired company moves onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems, and the integration plan for all three.

gate.label: Go/no-go on cutover
gate.decision: Go or no-go on moving the first company onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Move the first company's sales, purchasing and finance onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems and confirm they run.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the first-company result and the integration plan to take to the board?

workstreams.name: Current state, two companies
workstreams.answers: How do sales, purchasing and finance run today at two acquired companies, and how do they differ from Grupo Vale?
activities: Interview the people who run sales, purchasing and finance
Review operational data and documents for each process
Compare each process with Grupo Vale's own way of working

workstreams.name: Current state, third company
workstreams.answers: How do sales, purchasing and finance run today at the third acquired company, compared with Grupo Vale?
activities: Interview the people who run sales, purchasing and finance
Review operational data and documents for each process
Compare each process with Grupo Vale and the first two

workstreams.name: Gap ranking and alignment
workstreams.answers: Which gaps between the acquired companies and Grupo Vale come first, and do the stakeholders agree?
activities: Rank the differences from Grupo Vale by effect and effort
Agree the priority gaps with the CEO, CFO and company heads

workstreams.name: Move design by company
workstreams.answers: How should each acquired company's sales, purchasing and finance move onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
activities: Detail each company's move with its leaders, two at a time
Map each process and system gap to the change it needs
Check each design with the people who will run it

workstreams.name: Integration plan and risks
workstreams.answers: What integration plan for the three companies, with sequence and risks, can the board approve?
activities: Set the sequence for moving the three companies
Log the integration risks with owners and actions
Review the plan with the CEO, CFO and company heads

workstreams.name: Cutover readiness
workstreams.answers: Are the first company's data, test results and trained users ready for cutover?
activities: Rehearse and reconcile the data migration for each system
Run integrated test and user acceptance by process area
Train each process area team on Grupo Vale's processes

workstreams.name: First-company cutover
workstreams.answers: Do the first company's sales, purchasing and finance run on Grupo Vale's processes and systems after cutover?
activities: Cut over the first company's process areas, two at a time
Train and coach area teams; close issues after cutover
Confirm each area runs on Grupo Vale's systems

workstreams.name: Integration plan check
workstreams.answers: What does the first company's cutover change in the integration plan the board will be asked to approve?
activities: Update the plan's sequence and risks with cutover results
Review the updated plan with the CEO, CFO and company heads

deliverables.name: Current-state comparison with Grupo Vale, two companies
Current-state comparison with Grupo Vale, third company
Ranked gaps and agreed priorities for design go/no-go
Move design for each acquired company
Integration plan with risks and company move designs
Cutover readiness record for the first company
Go-live record and run confirmation by process area
First-company result and updated integration plan

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the work and secure data access
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Confirm access to each company's sales, purchasing and finance data and people?
agenda: Present the three phases and the dates of each meeting
Discuss the data and people needed from each company
Confirm access and one contact per company

events.label: Check-in: current state
events.purpose: Review current state of all three companies
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Which differences from Grupo Vale should the gap ranking cover?
agenda: Present the current-state comparisons for all three companies
Discuss where each company differs from Grupo Vale
Align on what the gap ranking covers in weeks 5-6

events.label: Go/no-go on design
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Go ahead with design on the agreed priority gaps in sales, purchasing and finance?
agenda: Present the ranked gaps and agreed priorities
Review the current-state comparisons behind the ranking
Decide whether design starts on the priority gaps

events.label: Go/no-go on cutover
events.purpose: Decide whether to move the first company
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Go or no-go on moving the first company onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
agenda: Present the move design for each acquired company
Review the integration plan and its risks
Decide go or no-go on moving the first company

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the result, prepare for the board
attendees: Heads of the three acquired companies
events.decision: Approve the first-company result and the integration plan to take to the board?
agenda: Present the go-live record and run confirmation by process area
Review the cutover readiness record and the updated integration plan
Decide whether to take the result and plan to the board

deadline.text: Before the board meeting on 29 January 2027

architect_notes: The work counted needs 24-37 weeks, more than the 12 planned: cut scope, run more at once, or extend.
Engagement length is assumed: phases are cut to the 12 weeks before the 29 January 2027 board meeting, but the work sizes at 24-37 weeks.
Shortfall against 12 weeks: Design gets 3 of 5-9 sized weeks, Implementation 3 of 13-20, so first-company cutover cannot finish by the board meeting.
Conflict: the board approves the plan after these phases, yet Implementation moves the first company onto Grupo Vale's systems before it; confirm that order.
Implementation units are the architect's estimates, including three assumed first-company systems to migrate; confirm 3-4 weeks per process area and the system count.
Implementation is sized for the first company only, as the brief states; which company goes first is not named and must be confirmed.

sub_questions.question: How do sales, purchasing and finance work today at each acquired company, compared with Grupo Vale?
How should each acquired company's sales, purchasing and finance move onto Grupo Vale's processes and systems?
What integration plan for the three companies, with sequence and risks, can the board approve?
Do the first company's sales, purchasing and finance run on Grupo Vale's processes and systems after cutover?

drivers.evidence: Grupo Vale has bought three regional food distributors

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Unit diagnosed (interviews, process walk-throughs, workload and cost baseline)

phases.why: Two companies are diagnosed side by side, then the third before gaps are ranked; sales, purchasing and finance are covered in each walk-through.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Unit-level design detailed with the unit's leaders

phases.why: Units designed two at a time, then plan and review. Minimum is below typical 6-10: no new target model, Grupo Vale's own is the target.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Data migration rehearsed and reconciled for one first-company system
Integrated test and user acceptance across the first company's process areas
User training for one first-company process area team
First-company process area cut over to Grupo Vale's processes and systems
First-company stabilization after cutover, with open issues closed

phases.why: No Implementation phase in the archetype. Migration, testing and training first, then areas cut over two at a time at the first company, then stabilization.

sizing.levers: Moving first-company cutover and stabilization after the board meeting saves 8-11 weeks; running all three process areas at once or diagnosing two companies saves less.
